response.record_grain: One grant award record: a single (grant programme, grant round, recipient, project, amount approved) entry from the Opendatasoft JSON export.
response.grain_rationale: The top-level JSON array is the record list; each flat object is one published award entry. The 'index' field is an export ordinal, not a durable business key, so the record id is constructed from stable award attributes after Unicode NFKC, dash/apostrophe folding and case-folding.

record_id.rationale: No stable publisher key exists; the award is identified by programme, round, published recipient, project text and amount. 'index' is an export ordinal and is excluded. Key inputs are normalised (Unicode NFKC, dash/apostrophe folding, case-fold) before hashing so that re-published rows with typographic dash or apostrophe variants produce the same record id.

fields.rationale: Published award amount; parsed as decimal. It is an award amount, not recipient income. Currency is inferred as AUD from the Brisbane City Council publisher jurisdiction and is not source-stated; flagged as inferred.
Publisher's round/financial-year label for the award cycle, kept as text.
Free-text project description owned by the award; not converted to an industry or sector code.

Recipient string as published; may be a natural person or organisation, so it is award-level matching evidence, not a legal name. May contain personal data when the recipient is a natural person, but is not always personal.

ABN recorded against the award recipient; checksum-validated. Presence does not establish company status or legal form, so it stays award-level until the recipient is resolved. Checksum-invalid values are nulled and reported separately from absence.

Published programme label under which the award was made. Where the publisher appends a ward/locality suffix, the suffix is a delivery location variant of the same scheme and is recorded separately in dyn.grant_programme.locality_variant.

The combined grant_list field prefixes a short programme code before the comma; extracted as the programme code. Only emitted when the grant_list label matches the grant field after Unicode NFKC, dash/apostrophe folding and case-folding; mismatches are flagged and the code is withheld.
Publisher's broader programme group/category, kept in publisher wording.

Ward/locality suffix appended to the programme label (e.g. Coorparoo, Bracken Ridge, Northgate), recorded separately so the programme can be keyed on the scheme name rather than the ward-scoped label. A delivery location, not a distinct scheme.

grant_award.rationale: Award record identified by programme, round, published recipient, project and amount, with key inputs normalised (Unicode NFKC, dash/apostrophe folding, case-fold) before hashing for cross-snapshot stability.

grant_programme.rationale: Programme identified by its published label; code, group and locality variant are attributes of the same programme. Ward/locality suffixes are recorded separately in dyn.grant_programme.locality_variant so the programme can be keyed on the scheme name rather than the ward-scoped label.

relationships.rationale: Each award is made under the programme named in the grant field.

unmapped.reason: Export row ordinal that may change between snapshots; not a stable business key, so it is not modelled. A deterministic record id is constructed from stable award attributes instead.

response.notes: Recipients mix individuals and organisations; no business entity role is declared because recipient identity is unresolved. entity.abn, ext.entity.holder_kind and RECEIVES_GRANT may be populated downstream only after recipient resolution and ABN checksum validation; RECEIVES_GRANT is intentionally unpopulated in this pass. Amounts are award amounts, not business income. Currency AUD is inferred from the Brisbane City Council publisher jurisdiction and is not source-stated. No source-stated observation date exists; observed_at falls back to the snapshot retrieval time and is documented as such, distinct from ingested_at. Dataset licence is CC-BY-4.0 per metadata.
